events.title: Emperor Galba murdered in the Roman Forum
events.description: Praetorians loyal to Otho killed the elderly Galba after just seven months as emperor. Otho, then Vitellius and finally Vespasian took power in the turmoil known as the Year of the Four Emperors.
events.html: Praetorians loyal to Otho killed the elderly Galba after just seven months as emperor. Otho, then Vitellius and finally Vespasian took power in the turmoil known as the Year of the Four Emperors.

events.title: Elizabeth I is crowned at Westminster Abbey
events.description: Elizabeth, daughter of Henry VIII and Anne Boleyn, was crowned on a date chosen by her astrologer John Dee. Her 44-year reign saw a Protestant settlement, the Armada's defeat and a flowering of literature.
events.html: Elizabeth, daughter of Henry VIII and Anne Boleyn, was crowned on a date chosen by her astrologer John Dee. Her 44-year reign saw a Protestant settlement, the Armada's defeat and a flowering of literature.

events.title: Truce of Jam Zapolski ends Russia's war with Poland-Lithuania
events.description: Ivan the Terrible gave up his conquests in Livonia to Stefan Batory's Polish-Lithuanian Commonwealth. The truce ended Russia's long attempt to win a foothold on the Baltic.
events.html: Ivan the Terrible gave up his conquests in Livonia to Stefan Batory's Polish-Lithuanian Commonwealth. The truce ended Russia's long attempt to win a foothold on the Baltic.

events.title: British Museum opens to the public
events.description: Founded on the collections of the physician Sir Hans Sloane, the British Museum opened in Montagu House, Bloomsbury. It was one of the first national museums open to all 'studious and curious persons'.

events.title: Vermont declares itself an independent republic
events.description: Settlers in the New Hampshire Grants declared independence as New Connecticut, renamed Vermont that summer. The republic outlawed adult slavery and joined the United States as the 14th state in 1791.
events.html: Settlers in the New Hampshire Grants declared independence as New Connecticut, renamed Vermont that summer. The republic outlawed adult slavery and joined the United States as the 14th state in 1791.

events.title: Thomas Nast's cartoon links the Democrats with a donkey
events.description: Nast's cartoon 'A Live Jackass Kicking a Dead Lion' in Harper's Weekly portrayed anti-war Democrats as a donkey. The donkey later became the accepted symbol of the Democratic Party.
events.html: Nast's cartoon 'A Live Jackass Kicking a Dead Lion' in Harper's Weekly portrayed anti-war Democrats as a donkey. The donkey later became the accepted symbol of the Democratic Party.

events.title: Rosa Luxemburg and Karl Liebknecht murdered in Berlin
events.description: After the defeat of the Spartacist uprising, the two communist leaders were seized and killed by Freikorps soldiers. The murders deepened the bitter split on the German left.
events.html: After the defeat of the Spartacist uprising, the two communist leaders were seized and killed by Freikorps soldiers. The murders deepened the bitter split on the German left.

events.title: Martin Luther King Jr. is born in Atlanta
events.description: Born Michael King Jr., the son of a Baptist minister, he became the leading voice of the American civil rights movement. He received the Nobel Peace Prize in 1964 and was assassinated in 1968.

events.title: The Pentagon is completed in Arlington, Virginia
events.description: Built in just 16 months, the five-sided headquarters of the US War Department was dedicated. With some 6.5 million square feet of floor space, it was the world's largest office building.
events.html: Built in just 16 months, the five-sided headquarters of the US War Department was dedicated. With some 6.5 million square feet of floor space, it was the world's largest office building.

events.title: Nixon suspends offensive action against North Vietnam
events.description: Citing progress in the Paris peace talks, Richard Nixon halted US bombing and mining of North Vietnam. The Paris Peace Accords, signed twelve days later, ended direct American involvement in the war.
